name: Nordic Social Democracy
summary: Nordic social democracy pairs a competitive market economy and free trade with high taxes, universal tax-funded welfare services, strong trade unions and collective bargaining. It pursues reform through parliamentary democracy rather than revolution, and treats gender equality, secular public life and class cooperation as central. Ownership is mostly private; the state regulates, redistributes and provides services.
scope: The Nordic model as developed by the Swedish Social Democrats (Branting, Per Albin Hansson's folkhem, Palme) and echoed in Denmark, Norway, Finland and Iceland, as it exists today. The 1882 founding programme is used only as a historical contrast, because the party later dropped its goal of abolishing wage labour. Excludes the revolutionary and Third Way variants.

keyFigures.name: Hjalmar Branting
keyFigures.role: Led the Swedish Social Democrats from its founding to 1925, favouring reform over revolution

keyFigures.name: Per Albin Hansson
keyFigures.role: Introduced the folkhem concept in 1928 and led the party into its long period of government

keyFigures.name: Olof Palme
keyFigures.role: Party leader in the 1970s and 80s, associated with the Swedish model and an internationalist foreign policy

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Nordic model's healthcare is universal and largely tax-funded, and Sweden's state-provided universal care was enacted in 1947-55 under the Social Democrats.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nordic wages are set by collective bargaining and Sweden and Denmark have no statutory minimum wage, so adherents favour higher pay via unions rather than a legal minimum.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The model is a market economy but rests on state regulation, redistribution and public services, so adherents deny that markets simply outperform governments.

public-ownership.rationale: Folkhem Social Democrats moved to regulating rather than nationalising business, though Nordic states keep some utility and rail ownership (Norway most of all).

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nordic income taxes are progressive and the SAP has raised rates on high earners slightly, but the funding relies broadly on taxing middle incomes too.

unions-good.rationale: Nordic union density is 50-90% and the SAP has historic organic ties to the LO federation, treating strong unions as a pillar of the model.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights are accepted in a market economy but are subordinate to taxation, regulation and social goals in the Social Democratic view.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Social democracy is described as capitalism with state regulation; the folkhem period regulated rather than nationalised business.

cut-welfare.rationale: The welfare state is the defining achievement of the Nordic model and the Social Democrats built it as a central aim.

worker-ownership.rationale: The party retreated from the 1976 Meidner wage-earner funds that would have shifted ownership, and mainstream practice leaves most firms privately owned.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The sources do not address surveillance; Nordic social democrats value civil liberties but have accepted counter-terror laws, so a mild disagreement is estimated.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Nordic social democratic governments have generally kept restrictive drug policy (Sweden especially), though Denmark and Norway have decriminalisation debates.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Nordic states have hate-speech laws that social democrats support, but the sources say little about it.

strong-leader.rationale: Folkhem and the party's parliamentary, consensus tradition are built on democratic, collective politics, not strongman bypassing of institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: The ideology is built around a large state delivering welfare and public services, so a view that the state is harmful is the opposite.

limit-guns.rationale: Nordic countries tightly license guns and social democrats favour restriction, though hunting culture limits the fervour; sources say little.

empower-police-military.rationale: Sources do not address it; recent Swedish Social Democrats have backed more police and defence funding while the tradition stresses rehabilitation.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sweden's Social Democrats introduced the sex-purchase ban in 1999 from a gender-equality view; other Nordic parties differ, so mildly against legalisation.

decide-locally.rationale: Public services are delivered mainly via local government, but welfare standards are set nationally, so the position is mixed.

rehabilitation.rationale: Nordic criminal justice is known for rehabilitative aims, and social democrats have associated themselves with that tradition.

traditional-family.rationale: The model promotes dual-earner families with parental leave and public childcare rather than a traditional breadwinner structure.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The party supports freedom from discrimination by sexual orientation and Nordic states were early to legalise same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Nordic social democrats are strongly committed to gender equality and the Nordic states legalised abortion early.

more-religion-public.rationale: The party tradition is secular, even republican, and Nordic public life is among the least religious in the world.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The party opposes racism and discrimination but Nordic policy tends to be universal rather than race-targeted, so the answer is mild.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Nordic equality policy treats gender roles as changeable, but the sources do not state the philosophical claim.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Folkhem implied a national community, yet modern social democrats stress inclusion; adherents emphasise culture variously.

gradual-change.rationale: The party under Branting favoured reform over revolution and has pursued incremental change through parliament.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The Swedish party tightened immigration rules after 2015 while the tradition stresses solidarity, and the sources are thin on this.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The party backed the UN tradition and Palme-era internationalism and promoted EU membership.

free-trade.rationale: The Nordic model supports free trade as part of an open market economy, with social protections to cushion losers.

nation-first.rationale: Palme-era foreign policy stressed solidarity and international cooperation over narrow national interest.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Social democrats back the UN and human rights but Swedish neutrality and Palme-era scepticism cut against intervention; views vary.

open-borders.rationale: Social democrats back generous refugee policy but link open borders with welfare-state sustainability, so they reject open borders as a goal.

limit-growth.rationale: The Nordic model relies on a growing productive economy to fund welfare; critics like Hickel note its footprint, but adherents do not seek limits on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The party pursues environmentalist policy with the Green and Left parties.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources say little; Nordic social democrats are pro-innovation but do not hold that technology solves most problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nordic social democrats have been divided on nuclear power, Sweden's party shifting from phase-out to accepting it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Branting led the party toward reform instead of revolution and even the 1882 programme describes lawful methods.

experts-over-public.rationale: The folkhem era saw technocratic planning by experts, but the party is also a mass democratic movement.

central-planning.rationale: Folkhem favoured a regulated, planned economy but not state-directed central planning, and Nordic economies are market-based.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets are accepted within a mixed economy with strong public and union involvement, which fits a market-with-public-guardrails view.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a Nordic social democratic programme; adherents rely on broad progressive taxes rather than a single land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Social democrats favour progressive taxation but several Nordic states abolished inheritance taxes (Sweden 2005), so only mild support.

basic-income.rationale: The model rests on work-linked insurance and active labour market policy, and Nordic social democrats have mostly rejected unconditional basic income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Nordic model supports free trade and small open economies depend on exports.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The party debated Meidner funds and investment planning, but modern practice relies mainly on market investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The tradition focuses on welfare and collective bargaining rather than property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Nordic model is built on wage labour with collective bargaining; abolition would contradict it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Nordic model supports a regulated market economy with public institutions; abolishing central banks is far from it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Nordic corporatism has employers, unions and government bargaining, but it is voluntary organisations rather than state-recognised price-setting bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: The party works within multi-party democracy and "democratic socialism" is its stated aim, so single-party rule is rejected.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Swedish party advocates abolishing the monarchy, though Nordic social democrats accept constitutional monarchies in practice.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy is core: the party's statutes speak of democratic socialism and expanding democracy to the economy.

direct-votes.rationale: The tradition favours parliamentary democracy, while referendums have been used on major questions such as EU entry.

workers-councils.rationale: The party is a parliamentary movement and rejects council rule.

right-to-secede.rationale: The sources do not address it; social democrats generally favour national unity within democratic states.

natural-rulers.rationale: The 1882 programme aims at equal rights and abolition of class rule, rejecting innate fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Commitment to lawful, parliamentary reform; though the party has not always been pacifist on principle.

war-builds-character.rationale: Palme-era and neutrality traditions reject glorification of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Swedish party backed disestablishing the Church (done 2000) and secular public life.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The tradition is secular and democratic.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Nordic model relies on strong public provision of justice and security.

military-superiority.rationale: Swedish social democracy tradition has been neutrality and disarmament diplomacy under Palme rather than military superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The party opposes racism and favours egalitarian, inclusive citizenship.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Folkhem marked a move from class struggle to class cooperation, though the 1882 programme used class language.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Strong egalitarianism and redistribution aim to reduce inequality of outcomes, not only of opportunity, though without full equalisation.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Nordic states recognise Sami parliaments, and social democrats broadly support Sami rights, but the sources say little.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not a Nordic social democratic theme; the sources are silent.

civilizational-union.rationale: The party supports the UN and EU but not union on religious-civilisational lines.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Folkhem stresses solidarity, cooperation and helpfulness over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Folkhem stresses community, but the party also upholds individual rights and democracy.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmentalist policy is supported, but intrinsic-value philosophy is not a party tenet.

limit-population.rationale: Nordic policy supports family policy for birthrates and does not endorse population limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The folkhem project was an industrial-modernist programme of progress.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources do not address it; the Nordic model values innovation while protecting workers from disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources do not address it; no party doctrine exists.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No documented position; adherents value accountable democratic and public administration.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No documented position; Nordic social democrats balance privacy and security.

restore-past-order.rationale: The ideology is progressive and reformist, building a new "people's home" rather than restoring an order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Nordic social democracy is pragmatic and consensus-oriented but also principled.

direct-action.rationale: The party works through elections, parliament and union bargaining.

means-match-ends.rationale: The party's stress on democratic means for democratic socialism implies means reflect ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The folkhem is an industrial welfare project, opposite to a foraging life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The Nordic model is a developed market economy with specialisation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Universal services are provided by need but wages reward work; mixed position.

production-for-use.rationale: The model is a market economy with private profit-seeking firms alongside public services.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The model accepts private profit within regulation; the 1882 programme's exploitation language was dropped with the shift to class cooperation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The party chose democratic reform and Hansson's class-cooperation folkhem, rejecting proletarian dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Nordic agriculture rests on private family farms and cooperatives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The party does not hold that capitalism inevitably produces great-power war.

taxation-theft.rationale: High taxation funding the welfare state is a foundation of the model.

harm-principle.rationale: The tradition values liberty but supports regulation beyond harm prevention such as public health.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Social democrats support collective rights such as bargaining and Sami rights alongside individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Sweden reintroduced conscription in 2017 under a Social Democratic government, while some Nordic parties opposed it historically.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democracy and voting are central, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is seen as a provider of rights-based public services, not a business with customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The folkhem and welfare state aim to give everyone the material means for real freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a party concern; they hold elected government as the chief political authority.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The party opposes racism and favours egalitarianism.

organic-representation.rationale: The party uses party-based parliamentary democracy though it has corporatist consultation with unions.

total-state.rationale: The ideology holds democratic socialism and a welfare state without directing every sphere of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The ideology is gradualist and rejects radical-rebirth rhetoric.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Palme-era and neutrality traditions reject expansionism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Social democracy is democratic and egalitarian, opposed to feudal loyalty ties.

bound-labor.rationale: The 1882 programme aims to abolish class rule and wage dependence.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: No stated position; mainstream reformist pragmatism treats knowledge as largely neutral.

universal-morality.rationale: Human rights universalism supported through the UN, but philosophy not stated.

single-common-good.rationale: Folkhem stressed cooperation, yet the party represents labour interests and bargains between groups.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Social democratic parties were historically sympathetic to Israel but are now divided over it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The party reinterpreted democratic socialism as expanding democracy in the economy, and Nordic codetermination gives employees board seats.

school-vouchers.rationale: Sweden's voucher system came from the 1990s reforms including Social Democratic governments, but the party has since turned sceptical of profit-making schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The party did fiscal consolidation after the 1990s crisis yet also supports countercyclical stimulus.

economic-freedom.rationale: Social democrats link political freedom to democracy and welfare more than to economic freedom.

national-self-determination.rationale: The party supported self-determination in the Palme-era anti-colonial stance and Nordic democracy.

force-without-un.rationale: Palme-era foreign policy respected international law and the UN.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secular but does not demand reason as the only guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nordic welfare is universal and residence-based, although debates exist on immigrant eligibility.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Active labour market policy and work-line (workfare in Iceland) make participation central.

class-collaboration.rationale: Folkhem was explicitly the shift from class struggle to class cooperation drawing on corporatist collaboration.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Free education and libraries are part of the welfare state, not to be sacrificed.

dominated-front.rationale: Not a party theme; neutrality rather than anti-Western fronts.

workers-nation.rationale: Social democracy has been internationalist in outlook and Palme-era in foreign solidarity, though parties operate nationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Nordic law is egalitarian, with parental leave and childcare to support gender equality.

ban-interest.rationale: Nordic market economy relies on credit.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The party opposes racism and discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Folkhem treats the democratic state as a vehicle for all, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The party has environmentalist policy, though Norway's Labour has defended oil.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Denmark has an assimilation policy while Sweden and Norway emphasise integration, so no single answer.

elite-replacement.rationale: The party opposes racism and conspiracy theories.

proportional-representation.rationale: Nordic states use proportional systems, and the party has supported them.

national-mission.rationale: Palme-era internationalism, not missionary promotion of national government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist policies and gender-equality measures presume structural inequalities.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nordic states rank high for trust and low corruption, and social democrats are part of the governing establishment.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Sweden's past sterilisation programme (a social democratic era policy) is now widely repudiated, and the modern party rejects eugenic coercion.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Human-rights stance implies accountability, though sources are silent.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The ideology is of an extensive welfare state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Hansson's folkhem speech says equality reigns in the home and the strong do not plunder the weak; the party opposes discrimination.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate not engaged by Nordic social democrats.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Nordic law is applied equally, the secular tradition.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The party's tradition is secular with freedom of religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a Nordic concern; animal welfare rules exist but a ban on cattle slaughter is foreign to it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Sweden has non-confessional religious education; the party supports secular schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Leninist doctrine alien to the democratic party.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Democratic socialism rests on popular democratic legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export-led small economies, but no doctrine of aiming for surpluses.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The model accepts the state's legitimate use of force through taxes and law, so absolute non-aggression is not held.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Nordic states are reluctant to ban parties, though militant-democracy ideas appear; no stated position.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Hansson's image of a home where the strong do not oppress the weak fits non-domination, but the republican theory is not stated in the sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Nordic parliamentary democracies have checks and the party operates within them, though doctrine is parliamentary supremacy.

vanguard-party.rationale: Branting's reformism and mass-party democratic socialism reject a revolutionary vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Universal welfare aims to relieve need and inequality, but the model is universal rather than targeted at the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public and cooperative housing are a welfare-state feature; the sources do not describe sell-offs as a goal.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strong unions and bargaining are central to the model, so restrictions on strikes run against it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Social democrats attribute poverty to social institutions and inequality, so reform of institutions is the remedy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The party's anti-racism and egalitarianism reject the claim, though debate on integration exists.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Elected parliamentary democracy is the norm.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rule-of-law democracy is valued, so suspension is opposed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Market economy with regulation; no documented stance on price caps.

party-controls-media.rationale: Multi-party democracy with free media; public service media are independent.

party-commands-army.rationale: Democratic civilian control of the armed forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Nordic states have moderate residence requirements and the party has favoured integration, though tightened rules recently.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not part of mainstream social democracy, which accepts normal MP salaries.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Social democratic parties typically have strong parliamentary discipline, but sources are silent on doctrine.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Under Persson, Sahlin and Lindh the party promoted EU membership.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The party advocates ending the monarchy's role and parliamentary government.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Social democracy supported national defence and neutrality, not defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Nordic cultural policy supports free expression.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Parliamentary systems have no fixed presidential terms; no doctrine.

recall-officials.rationale: Not a Nordic parliamentary practice; no support documented.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Sweden's party backed neutrality historically but supported NATO accession in 2022.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Nordic housing includes strong rental sectors and cooperatives.

people-in-arms.rationale: Nordic militia and conscription traditions exist but doctrine not stated.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Folkhem was an urbanising industrial project.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Free education at all levels is a social democratic achievement.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Anti-racism supports it but the sources do not state the philosophical claim.

death-penalty.rationale: Nordic states abolished capital punishment and the party's egalitarian human-rights values oppose it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality is a core policy and Nordic schools teach sex education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Mixed; gender-equality feminists in the party support some limits, but no documented line.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nordic states combine rules; no documented stance.

minority-language-support.rationale: Sami and minority language rights are supported in Nordic policy.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Nordic liberal social values, but not a documented party theme.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Palme-era solidarity with the Third World, but no documented debt policy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: No documented position; Nordic constitutions evolve through parliament.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sweden has been a generous aid donor under Social Democrats and Palme-era solidarity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The party supported nuclear disarmament under Palme.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The party advocates ending the monarchy but parliamentary government; direct election is not a party aim.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The Social Democrats accepted central bank independence in Sweden in the 1990s.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Folkhem and regulated business imply property serves social ends.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Social democrats criticised the USSR, but the label is a left-communist debate.

collective-defense.rationale: Sweden's party backed NATO accession in 2022, a collective-defence alliance, after its neutrality tradition.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Secular, but not hostile to churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Nordic monarchs are nonpartisan symbols, though the party favours abolishing the monarchy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The party advocates abolishing the monarchy and is secular.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income taxes in the Nordic model are progressive.

character-from-environment.rationale: Social democratic reformism stresses social circumstances and education.

leader-cult.rationale: A democratic party hostile to leader cults.

equal-parenting.rationale: Gender-equal parenting is supported via parental leave but court presumptions are not documented.

land-redistribution.rationale: Nordic agriculture rests on private farms; redistribution isn't the programme.

refugee-return.rationale: Palme-era solidarity with refugees and Palestinians but nothing documented.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The party's secular tradition and disestablishment of the Church make state punishment for leaving a religion unthinkable.

common-currency.rationale: Sweden's party promoted EU membership but the euro was rejected by referendum in 2003 and the party stayed divided.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nordic cooperation exists, but no political union doctrine.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Equal rights and anti-discrimination are favoured.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The 1882 programme used economic language, but the modern party does not hold a historical-materialist doctrine.

ban-cartels.rationale: Fair competition rules are part of a regulated market economy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Sweden's 1990s crisis response used guarantees; no stated doctrine.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Nordic traditions favour parliamentary supremacy, but human-rights norms limit it.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Party applies gender quotas and measures to increase women's political participation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Nordic economies are open and trade-dependent.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Social democrats back labour protections and Nordic internationalism.

moral-incentives.rationale: Wage bargaining and market incentives remain.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The party advocates abolishing the monarchy and favours equal rights.

patriotic-education.rationale: Folkhem had national solidarity, but nothing on school patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Nordic policy does not use racial preferences; no stated position.

public-money-creation.rationale: No documented position; market economy norm.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Modern social democracy is capitalism with regulation and redistribution that survives crises, as Bernstein's revisionism held.

elective-rulers.rationale: Abolition of monarchy favours elected rulers.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Social democratic doctrine does not address a right of resistance; the answer is a neutral placeholder for a parliamentary tradition.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary democracy is the party's route to reform.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Environmental and animal welfare policy is supported.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Social democrats favour state-guaranteed welfare as rights rather than elite charity.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist cultural theory not held by Nordic social democrats.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian theory not a party tenet.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory not adopted, though solidarity with development exists.

party-own-road.rationale: Social democrats are independent national parties.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Nordic countries do not press revanchism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Sami parliament consults but no leadership claim.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Social democrats opposed both Nazism and Soviet communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not documented; party would accept scholarship.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Equality policy sometimes addresses boys' schooling but no documented stance.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Feminist policies stress violence against women.

paid-care-work.rationale: Public care and parental leave make care part of the welfare economy.

filial-duty.rationale: The Nordic welfare state transfers elder care to public provision, reducing reliance on filial duty.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Open economies with some state holdings; no doctrine.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The Swedish pension reform mixed a small premium pension within a public system under a social democratic government.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Nordic land is privately owned within a market economy, and use-based community tenure is not part of the model.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nordic economies are open to foreign capital and trade, so a ban on foreign land ownership is unlikely to be supported.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Nordic anti-discrimination law differs; no stated position.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Critics and Nordic ecological debates, though not a doctrine.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Denounced US war in Vietnam; respects sovereignty.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The open-economy, open-society Nordic model makes restricting foreign funding of NGOs and media unattractive to adherents.

job-guarantee.rationale: Active labour market policy and the work line, but not an employer-of-last-resort doctrine.

democratic-peace.rationale: Party faith in democracy and internationalism.

industrial-unions.rationale: Swedish LO blue-collar federation organised by industry.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The party's anti-racism and opposition to discrimination exclude ethnic conspiracy claims.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: No stated position; Nordic law recognises marriage and cohabitation.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Sweden's principle of public access dates from 1766 and is embedded in the Nordic model.

local-production.rationale: Small, trade-dependent Nordic economies rely on exports and imports, so localism is not a goal.

informal-organisation.rationale: A mass party with union ties.

religious-nation.rationale: The secular party tradition defines the nation by citizenship, not shared religion.

defeat-communism.rationale: Social democrats opposed Soviet communism but practised coexistence and détente.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Denmark relies on private provision and Sweden privatised some services after the 1990s crisis within public funding.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Accepts markets and capitalism as productive within reform.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Parental leave and childcare reform the economic structure of work.

socialized-care.rationale: Public childcare and elder care are core Nordic services.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Nordic cooperatives exist, but society is organised through the state.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The folkhem is described as the Swedish Middle Way between capitalism and socialism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Social democrats stand in the anti-racist, anti-fascist tradition and reject denial as plainly false.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Opposes discrimination based on sexual orientation.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: A secular democratic party with free expression traditions would not punish blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The party's Palme-era stance was anti-colonial and for international solidarity.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A secular party does not hold religious military obligations.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Democratic socialism rejects removing rulers by force on religious grounds; change comes through elections.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Democratic socialism as expansion of democracy, including at work.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: No stated adoption of intersectional theory.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anti-discrimination policy; Sweden legalised gender recognition early.

assisted-dying.rationale: Nordic social democrats are divided and conscience-driven.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The party defines itself on the centre-left.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxian concept in the 1882 programme era, not central today.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The party's anti-racism and equal-rights stance rejects the claim that a religion is incompatible with Nordic values.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Democratic socialism rests on popular sovereignty and a secular state, not divine authority.

social-market-economy.rationale: The model is a market economy combined with social protection, regulation and collective bargaining.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Sweden's neutrality ended with NATO accession in 2022 under party support.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The party seeks abolition of the monarchy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Nordic model uses a conventional banking sector within a regulated market economy.

property-franchise.rationale: Universal suffrage was a central labour-movement cause.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Press subsidies in Nordic states, but no stated doctrine.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Parliamentary democracy and rule through publicly enacted laws is the framework in which the party works.

racial-franchise.rationale: Universal suffrage was a founding labour-movement demand, and the party opposes racial discrimination.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Secular equality before the law rules out restrictions on marriage by religion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The party's anti-racism and anti-discrimination stance rejects boycotts aimed at a minority.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Social democrats are secular and take no party line on how religions should interpret their doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Redistribution and union counterweight aim to prevent power concentration.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nordic model uses public safety institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The Nordic states are not deeply divided, and the sources record no party doctrine on consociationalism.

term-limits.rationale: Parliamentary systems built around party lists have no tradition of term limits, so adherents likely see no need.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources record no stance on extinction-risk policy, so a neutral placeholder is used.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Gender equality; Church of Sweden ordains women.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nordic states grant local voting rights to resident foreigners.

rent-control.rationale: Tenant protection and negotiated rent systems.

abolish-ip.rationale: A market economy with private firms and innovation relies on patents and copyright, which the model does not seek to abolish.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Neutrality tradition but NATO accession changed the position.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The 1882 programme and labour tradition favour rewards from work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The party does not teach pacifism.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The sources record no party position on the philosophy of sex versus gender.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The sources record no stance on feminist category theory.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: A secular, pragmatic reform party sees politics as interest bargaining and policy, not a struggle of good and evil.

culture-before-state.rationale: The folkhem project used the state and legislation to transform society rather than waiting for cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Church of Sweden debates; no party doctrine.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A secular party has no position on judging religious texts by this criterion.

independent-unions.rationale: Nordic unions are voluntary and bargain independently, though historically tied to the party.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Democratic socialism via parliament; sources split on the label.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Local services mainly delivered via local government.

second-chamber.rationale: Sweden abolished its upper chamber in 1970 under a Social Democratic government, but the party's view is not stated.

municipal-property.rationale: The model leaves most firms private with public utilities and local services run by municipalities, not community ownership of production.

family-wage.rationale: Dual-earner model rather than family wage.

person-over-state.rationale: Folkhem emphasises community but respects individuals.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The party's secular tradition offers no doctrine of spiritual human nature, though it does not oppose religion.

gm-crops.rationale: No party doctrine on genetically engineered crops is recorded.

dense-cities.rationale: Environmentalist policy mildly favours compact urban living, but the sources record no explicit stance.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The party's egalitarian, anti-racist universalism rejects organising politics by racial group.

racial-pride.rationale: The party's anti-racism makes racial pride a suspect idea, though it would not be a main concern.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The party's civic and inclusive notion of citizenship rejects defining a nation by language alone.

communal-electorates.rationale: Universal suffrage with common proportional lists is the standard, not separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: No such view is part of social democracy, which is internationalist and conspiracy-free.

free-public-college.rationale: Sweden made education free at all levels under Social Democrats.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Feminist policy is framed around equality; the sources do not state an essentialist claim about women's values.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Democratic and Palme-era internationalist values mildly favour transparency in diplomacy, though no doctrine is recorded.

capital-controls.rationale: Small open Nordic economies favour free capital movement within regulation.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A democratic rule-of-law state holds the monopoly of force, which social democrats accept.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Employers, unions and government negotiate workplace rules, with Sweden using national-level bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Earned income tax credits used in Sweden, but no stated doctrine.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Sweden adopted fiscal rules after the 1990s crisis with party support.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Branting's reformist line aims to use the democratic state, not destroy it.

nature-as-capital.rationale: No party doctrine on valuing ecosystems as capital is recorded.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Free tuition model in place; no stated doctrine.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The sources record no such analysis; regional redistribution through taxes is the Nordic practice.

public-service-media.rationale: Public service broadcasting is a Nordic institution.

religions-one-truth.rationale: A secular party has no position on the unity of religions.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agricultural subsidies exist in Nordic countries; no stated doctrine.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Under Palme the party favoured disarmament, and Sweden has no nuclear weapons.

workers-own-party.rationale: The party was founded as a workers' party.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Nordic law is egalitarian, with gender equality a central party commitment.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmentalism is supported but the party also defends liberty, so adherents would weigh the two case by case.

voter-id.rationale: No Nordic voter ID requirement tradition.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Democratic emphasis, though social democrats also stress social democracy.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The party is secular and feminist but records no claim about religion as a major cause of oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: The party's anti-racism is consistent with this view, but the sources record no explicit position.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: A secular party has no doctrine of scriptural inerrancy.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Gender-equality commitments imply women's participation in any self-government arrangements, but the sources do not discuss it.

indirect-election.rationale: The party works within directly elected parliaments and has backed proportional representation.

national-church-status.rationale: Disestablished the Church of Sweden in 2000.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: No party position is recorded; universal equal rights and free movement within Nordic states weigh against restrictions.

equal-conscription.rationale: Sweden's gender-neutral conscription (2010/2017) under a Social Democratic government.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Social democratic nationalism is civic and welfare-centred rather than a spiritual tie to land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The party is committed to democratic rule of law and abolished the death penalty.

close-ties-china.rationale: The party's Western-aligned, human-rights-oriented foreign policy makes a China-first tilt unlikely.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Norway's state oil funds share common wealth, but no theory.

self-ownership.rationale: Self-ownership is a libertarian doctrine not addressed in Nordic social democracy, which accepts taxation and bodily-autonomy rights alike.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Indirect taxes are a revenue base, though the 1882 programme opposed them and the party cut food VAT.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The party is itself a mass party and works with unions and interest groups, so it rejects bypassing them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Fair competition rules are part of the model, so adherents mildly oppose special privileges.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The secular party tradition prefers politics organised around class and policy, not denomination.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The folkhem was a forward-looking modernising project rather than a return to ancestral values.

missingStatements.text: Governments should provide paid parental leave and publicly subsidised childcare so that both parents can work.
missingStatements.rationale: Parental leave and subsidised childcare are described as defining Nordic policies that support continuous full-time work for both sexes.

notes: Many answers are low-confidence because the sources describe the model's institutions rather than party positions on culture-war or foreign-policy questions. Nordic parties differ (Denmark's assimilation policy, Norway's state ownership); the profile follows the Swedish mainstream.
